title: Doctor exact runtime and tool version reporting
description:
Objective: give the production doctor surface an exact engine/runtime/tool/component version report, so that consumers can compare a declared pin against an observed version and get an explicit verdict instead of having no subject to assert against.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Three BLOCKED HIGH tasks each independently measured the same gap and each named it as their own prerequisite "B". Authorised by governor-f70d1157 at 12:25:15Z on the measurement below; created by worker-5981deec rather than an architect because the gap was measured symbol by symbol and the DoD needs no judgement the measurement does not already supply.

CONSUMERS (name these rather than re-measuring; all three are BLOCKED on this among other things):
- task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275 Linux effect conformance. Its DoD 3 is "packaging uses pinned engine/runtime, doctor reports exact versions"; its block records the doctor clause as having no subject.
- task-e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 macOS effect conformance. Same DoD, same block: "reports its schema version but has no exact engine/runtime version surface".
- task-9449ce65fae544ef9809691ec079f599 Release supply-chain gate. Needs DOCTOR compatibility evidence bound to a source commit for its DoD 3; full audit in comment-81bfe196d1f2418588c44f66b705966c.

MEASURED STATE AT HEAD 1ce0059de305e9e8f13f099daa1b9c5249b34071 (verified independently by governor-f70d1157 before authorising):
- apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-commands.ts is 229 lines. "schemaVersion" appears only at :54 as a frozen REQUEST_KEYS entry and at :174 in the exact-shape check. It is the REQUEST's schema version, not a runtime version.
- No nodeVersion, no process.version, no engine/tool/component inventory anywhere in the file. The only "runtime" hits are RuntimeCommandKind and prose.
- Repo-wide: grep for "nodeVersion|node_version|pnpmVersion" across every packages/*/src and apps/*/src returns ZERO files.
- The pins the report must observe against already exist: .node-version = 24.16.0; root package.json packageManager = pnpm@11.0.8; engines = { node ">=24.16.0 <25", pnpm "11.0.8" }.

SIZE CONSTRAINT, MEASURED — READ BEFORE PLANNING. doctor-commands.ts is already 229 physical lines against a 250 target. This work does NOT fit inside it. Put the version surface in a sibling module under apps/daemon/src/recovery/ and have doctor-commands.ts compose it, exactly as the epic's per-file cap requires. Do not grow doctor-commands.ts toward 400.

HOUSE SHAPE TO FOLLOW, so this composes instead of inventing a second style. doctor-commands.ts already establishes it: a frozen DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS array; a frozen DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES array; layered refusals where each stage names its own layer (BOUNDED_JSON for the decoder, DOCTOR for the doctor) so a reader can tell which one answered; a frozen discriminated result union carrying ok/outcome/layer/code; and PROPOSED_COMMANDS typed Readonly<Record<string, RuntimeCommandKind>> so a typo is a build failure. A new command kind belongs in DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS, and any new refusal code belongs in DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES — a code emitted in production that is absent from the frozen vocabulary is a defect this board has already been bitten by twice.

NOT IN SCOPE: packaging, publishing, signing, SBOM, distribution manifests or any OS-conformance execution. This task ships the version-reporting capability only. It makes no claim about any OS.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/ (the new version module, its .js bridge, its tests, and the composition edge in doctor-commands.ts). Do not edit root package.json, .node-version, or any consumer task's files.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck
definitionOfDone: The doctor reports the exact OBSERVED Node runtime version, pnpm version, and platform/arch, read from the running process and the live tool rather than restated as literals in source. A test proves the value is observed by asserting it equals the value the test itself reads from the same production accessor, never by comparing against a hard-coded version string — a literal comparison passes while the reader is broken, which is the exact failure the report exists to prevent.

The doctor reports the DECLARED pins separately from the observed values, sourced from .node-version and root package.json packageManager/engines, and emits an explicit per-pin verdict comparing declared against observed. Declared and observed are never merged into one field, because a consumer that cannot see both cannot tell a satisfied pin from an unread one.

Every version, tool or component the doctor cannot read is typed UNKNOWN with a stable code drawn from the frozen DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES vocabulary and the layer that refused, per epic rail 4. It is never omitted from the report, never defaulted to a plausible value, and never allowed to read as satisfied. A test asserts the specific code and the refusing layer for each unreadable case, not merely that the result was not ok.

The report enumerates the daemon plus the declared workspace components with their versions, and asserts a positive non-zero component count so a report that swept nothing fails instead of passing. The report is a frozen value and the new command kind is registered in DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS, with any new refusal code registered in DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES so no production code can emit a value absent from the frozen vocabulary.

The new module carries its .js bridge in the same commit and is proven loadable in a PLAIN NODE process, not only under vitest — vitest resolves NodeNext .js specifiers back to .ts and structurally cannot detect a missing bridge. Every production file touched stays at or below 250 physical lines.
taskRails: This is a production capability task, not a conformance or acceptance task. It ships the version-reporting surface and makes NO claim about any operating system. Do not add OS conformance assertions, fault schedules, or packaging evidence here — those belong to the three consumer tasks.

Observed values must be READ, never restated. A version literal written into source and compared against itself is a reimplementation of the thing under test, and epic rail 6 makes that a defect regardless of how green the suite is. Verify each reader by mutating it and confirming the named test goes red.

doctor-commands.ts is 229 lines against a 250 target. Add a sibling module and compose it; do not grow that file. If the version surface itself approaches 250, split it again rather than heading for 400.

Missing, unreadable or ambiguous version information stays UNKNOWN with a stable code and the refusing layer. It never gains authority and never renders as a satisfied pin. An UNKNOWN that is declared and reasoned is valid evidence; a manufactured green is not.

implementationPlan.description: PURE CONTRACT. Create apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-version-contract.ts and its one-line bridge doctor-version-contract.js (`export * from "./doctor-version-contract.ts";`). No IO, no process reads, no fs. Contents: `DOCTOR_VERSION_REPORT_VERSION = "moe-doctor-version-report/1"`; frozen `DOCTOR_VERSION_LAYERS` = [DOCTOR_VERSION, DOCTOR_VERSION_HOST] so the pure comparator's refusal is distinguishable from the host reader's; frozen `PIN_VERDICTS` = [SATISFIED, MISMATCHED, UNKNOWN]; frozen `VERSION_PIN_KINDS` = [NODE_RUNTIME, PNPM_TOOL, ENGINES_NODE, ENGINES_PNPM]. Core type, and the shape that makes DoD 2 and DoD 3 mechanical: `ObservedValue = {known:true, value:string} | {known:false, code:DoctorErrorCode, layer:DoctorVersionLayer}` — an unreadable value is PRESENT, typed and coded, never omitted and never defaulted. Then `VersionPinVerdict {pin, declared: ObservedValue, observed: ObservedValue, verdict: PinVerdict}` keeping declared and observed as SEPARATE fields that are never merged; `ComponentEntry {name, version: ObservedValue}`; `DoctorVersionReport {reportVersion, observed:{node,pnpm,platform,arch}, declared:{nodeVersionFile,packageManager,enginesNode,enginesPnpm}, pins: readonly VersionPinVerdict[], components: readonly ComponentEntry[], componentCount:number}`; and the outcome interface `DoctorVersionsReported {ok:true, outcome:"VERSIONS_REPORTED", kind, report}` declared HERE so doctor-commands.ts imports the type rather than growing by a full interface. Pure functions: `comparePin(pin, declared, observed): VersionPinVerdict` — either side `{known:false}` yields UNKNOWN, never SATISFIED and never MISMATCHED, because a missing observation is not a disagreement; and `buildDoctorVersionReport(input): DoctorVersionReport` returning a deep-frozen value with `componentCount === components.length`. Handle the range pin explicitly: `engines.node` is `>=24.16.0 <25`, a RANGE, while `.node-version` is exact — either implement a narrow tested range check or return UNKNOWN with a stable code for that pin, but never string-compare a range against a version.
implementationPlan.note:
PURE CONTRACT landed. 249 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (against a 250 target), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0. Bridge written byte-exact as the sweep requires: `export * from "./doctor-version-contract.ts";`.

Shipped as planned: DOCTOR_VERSION_REPORT_VERSION, frozen DOCTOR_VERSION_LAYERS / PIN_VERDICTS / VERSION_PIN_KINDS, the ObservedValue two-arm union, VersionPinVerdict with declared and observed as separate fields, ComponentEntry, DoctorVersionReport, DoctorVersionsReported, comparePin and buildDoctorVersionReport. No IO, no process read, no fs.

FOUR DECISIONS WORTH REVIEW.

1. *** THE PLAN'S DOCTOR_PIN_MISMATCH IS NOT SHIPPED; DOCTOR_PIN_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED IS. *** No production path emits DOCTOR_PIN_MISMATCH — a mismatch is already carried by the `MISMATCHED` verdict, and VersionPinVerdict has no code field. Adding it would create exactly the DEAD vocabulary entry that mem:gotcha-daemon-refusal-code-vocabulary-drift names as the other direction of the same defect: a type guard stops an invented code but not a declared code nothing emits. DOCTOR_PIN_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED replaces it and is emitted for real, by compareRangePin on a range outside the supported grammar. It also gives the DOCTOR_VERSION layer a genuine production path — without it that layer would appear in no ObservedValue and the two-layer split would be an untested claim.

2. Codes live in the CONTRACT as DOCTOR_VERSION_ERROR_CODES, and step 5 will spread them into DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES rather than restate them. Restating is how the two lists drift; importing DoctorErrorCode the other way would close a type cycle between the two modules. Same reason DoctorVersionsReported types `kind` as the literal "doctor.report_versions" instead of DoctorCommandKind.

3. RANGE GRAMMAR IS DELIBERATELY NARROW: `>=<exact> <partial>`, which is what engines.node actually declares. Anything else returns a coded UNKNOWN rather than a guess. Never string-compares a range against a version.

4. DEEP FREEZE MADE ROBUST rather than caller-dependent. First cut froze the two groups with a shallow `Object.freeze({...observed})`, which leaves nested ObservedValues mutable whenever a caller builds them as raw literals instead of via the known()/unknown() factories — a report advertised as frozen with mutable interior. Now the groups are frozen BEFORE the pins are built, so the values each verdict aliases are already frozen, and componentCount is DERIVED from the array so a report cannot claim a sweep it did not perform.

BEHAVIOURAL SMOKE in plain Node (not vitest), all correct: declared "24.16.0\n" vs observed "v24.16.0" -> SATISFIED; "24.16.0\r\n" -> SATISFIED; 24.15.0 vs v24.16.0 -> MISMATCHED; unknown observed -> UNKNOWN (never SATISFIED); ">=24.16.0 <25" against v24.16.0 -> SATISFIED, v24.15.9 -> MISMATCHED, v25.0.0 -> MISMATCHED; "^24" -> declared becomes {known:false, DOCTOR_PIN_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED, DOCTOR_VERSION} with verdict UNKNOWN; packageManager "pnpm@11.0.8" -> "11.0.8".

The step-1 `v`-prefix finding is handled here and is the reason the first two cases pass; without the normalisation NODE_RUNTIME would read MISMATCHED on a correctly pinned host.

SIZE HEADROOM IS ONE LINE. At 249/250 this file cannot absorb another change. If steps 5-7 force one, I will take the split rather than trim behaviour — the comparison helpers (normalize, parseVersion, satisfiesRange, comparePin, compareRangePin, packageManagerVersion) move to doctor-version-compare.ts + bridge, which stays in the runtime tier by closure from this module.

Next: step 3, the red suites.

implementationPlan.description: RED SUITE FIRST (TDD). Create apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-version.test.ts against the not-yet-written readers. Vocabulary: `DOCTOR_VERSION_LAYERS`, `PIN_VERDICTS` and `VERSION_PIN_KINDS` each deep-equal a HAND-WRITTEN literal and are frozen — a list transcribed from the export under test asserts only that it equals itself. Observed values, per DoD 1 and task rail 2: assert `report.observed.node` is `{known:true}` and its value equals `process.version` as read by the TEST, and additionally matches /^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+/ so a hard-coded constant could not satisfy it; same treatment for platform and arch against `process.platform`/`process.arch`. For pnpm assert a two-branch disjunction — either `{known:true}` with a semver-shaped value, or `{known:false}` with code DOCTOR_TOOL_VERSION_UNREADABLE at layer DOCTOR_VERSION_HOST — plus an assertion that exactly one branch was taken, so it cannot pass by taking neither. Declared pins: reading a fixture root yields the exact `.node-version` and packageManager strings; a root with a missing or unparseable file yields `{known:false}` with DOCTOR_DECLARED_PIN_UNREADABLE at DOCTOR_VERSION_HOST; a `.node-version` with a trailing CRLF still compares SATISFIED. Comparator: SATISFIED on equality; MISMATCHED on a real disagreement, asserting the exact verdict AND that both declared and observed survive as separate fields; UNKNOWN whenever either side is unknown, asserted at layer DOCTOR_VERSION — which, paired with the host-layer cases above, is what proves the two layers are distinguishable. Components: sweep the real workspace and assert `componentCount > 0`, `componentCount === components.length`, and that `@moe/daemon` appears by name; a fixture root whose globs match nothing yields DOCTOR_COMPONENT_INVENTORY_EMPTY rather than an empty success; a declared-but-absent glob root (as `adapters/` really is) does not throw. Command edge: `doctor.report_versions` with no report supplied refuses with DOCTOR_VERSION_REPORT_ABSENT at layer DOCTOR; with a report supplied it returns outcome VERSIONS_REPORTED carrying a frozen report. Closed-vocabulary sweep: collect every code the suite produced into a Set, assert `size > 0` and that every member is present in the frozen DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES, so no production code can emit a value absent from the vocabulary. Finally the DoD 5 plain-Node proof: copy the `probe()` helper from runtime-entrypoint.test.ts and, in a REAL child Node process, `import("./src/recovery/doctor-version.node.js")` from the package root and CALL the reader, reporting the outcome as JSON — vitest rewrites `.js` specifiers back to `.ts`, so only a child process can detect a missing bridge.

RED SUITES WRITTEN. Two files, per the step-1 deviation, so the bridge sweep seeds both new modules as published units under direct test.

`doctor-version-contract.test.ts` — 26 tests, ALL PASSING, because the contract landed in step 2. Every vocabulary is deep-equalled against a HAND-TRANSCRIBED literal, never against the export under test.
`doctor-version.node.test.ts` — RED for the right reason: `Cannot find module './doctor-version.node.js'`. No cases ran, which is the correct starting state for step 4.

WHAT THE READER SPEC PINS, written before the readers exist:
- Observed node/platform/arch compared against process.version/platform/arch READ BY THE TEST, plus a /^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+/ shape assertion so a compiled-in constant cannot satisfy either half.
- pnpm as a two-branch disjunction with `expect([asValue, asUnknown].filter(Boolean)).toHaveLength(1)` — it cannot pass by taking neither branch. Asserting 11.0.8 would have been machine-dependent, since UNKNOWN is a legitimate answer on a host with no non-shim pnpm.
- Declared pins: real values read from disk by the test; missing .node-version, unparseable package.json, and an undiscoverable root each assert the exact code AND the refusing layer.
- Components: real workspace count > 0 and @moe/daemon present by name; a glob that matches nothing yields the code rather than a bare empty array; an absent glob root does not throw; an unparseable member manifest stays IN the inventory with a coded version.
- Closed-vocabulary sweep collects every code the suite actually produced and asserts membership in DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES, with a non-empty assertion first so a sweep of zero cannot pass.
- DoD 5 probe runs a REAL child Node process against `./src/recovery/doctor-version.node.js` and CALLS the reader, because a module can import cleanly and fail on first use.

ONE CONTRACT CHANGE THIS STEP FORCED, and it is a DoD 3 fix rather than a convenience. The planned shape had no way to carry an unreadable component inventory INTO the report: an empty `components` array is identical whether the sweep found nothing or could not run, and DoD 3 requires that anything the doctor cannot read is present in the report with a stable code, never omitted. Added `componentInventory: ObservedValue` to DoctorVersionReport and its input — known with the count, or unknown with DOCTOR_COMPONENT_INVENTORY_EMPTY and the refusing layer. Without it the second case would have read as a satisfied inventory, which is exactly what task rail 4 forbids.

SIZE. That field pushed the contract to 257, over the 250 target. I did NOT take the pre-approved split, because the overage was entirely comment prose, not behaviour: condensed six doc blocks, kept every WHY, and landed at 248 by `grep -c ''`. Behaviour is byte-for-byte what step 2 shipped plus the new field. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` reports ZERO errors under apps/daemon.

implementationPlan.description: NODE READERS — make it green. Create apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-version.node.ts and its one-line .node.js bridge, following the recovery-incarnation.node.ts precedent for the effectful half. Exports: `readObservedRuntime()` returning node/platform/arch from `process.version`/`process.platform`/`process.arch` — READ, never restated as a literal; `resolveRepoRoot(fromDir)` walking up from `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` to the directory holding pnpm-workspace.yaml, returning null rather than throwing; `readDeclaredPins(repoRoot)` parsing `.node-version` (trim trailing whitespace and CRLF before comparing, or every Windows pin reads MISMATCHED) and root package.json `packageManager` + `engines`; `readWorkspaceComponents(repoRoot)` resolving the workspace globs to each package.json name+version, tolerating a declared-but-absent root such as `adapters/` without throwing and without silently sweeping zero; `readPnpmVersion()` following the measured candidate ladder — `process.env.npm_execpath` when it ends .js/.cjs run via `process.execPath`, else `node_modules/pnpm/bin/pnpm.cjs` via `process.execPath`, else a PATH lookup for a REAL executable filtered through PATHEXT on win32 and explicitly excluding .cmd/.bat/.ps1 because Node 24 cannot spawn those with shell:false and a shell is not an option here. Every spawn: `shell:false`, `windowsHide:true`, bounded maxBuffer, explicit timeout, stdin ignored; accept exactly one semver-shaped line; an unresolvable executable, a non-zero exit, extra output, or a timeout each return `{known:false}` with DOCTOR_TOOL_VERSION_UNREADABLE at DOCTOR_VERSION_HOST. No spawn error may escape as a throw — the doctor must answer, not crash. Compose the whole thing in `collectDoctorVersionReport()` which calls the readers and hands the results to the pure `buildDoctorVersionReport`; the comparison authority stays in the contract module. Keep this file <=250 physical lines by `wc -l`; if it crosses, split the workspace sweep into `doctor-version-components.node.ts` + bridge — pre-approved, do not trim behaviour to fit.
implementationPlan.note:
NODE READERS GREEN. 44 of 45 version tests pass; the single remaining red is the closed-vocabulary sweep, which is precisely step 5's work — DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES does not yet carry the new codes. Nothing else is outstanding.

*** TOOK THE PRE-APPROVED SPLIT. *** First cut of doctor-version.node.ts measured 269 lines by `grep -c ''`, over DoD 5's hard 250. The plan pre-authorised splitting the workspace sweep rather than trimming behaviour, so that is what happened — no reader lost a case, no refusal path was removed.

Final sizes, all production files under the cap:
  doctor-version-contract.ts          248
  doctor-version.node.ts              169
  doctor-version-components.node.ts   129

The split line is filesystem-vs-process, not an arbitrary cut: doctor-version-components.node.ts holds root discovery, manifest reading and the workspace sweep; doctor-version.node.ts holds the process read, the declared pins, the pnpm spawn ladder and the composition. `resolveRepoRoot` and `readWorkspaceComponents` are re-exported by name from the node module so consumers and tests reach the whole boundary through one entry point rather than learning the split.

BRIDGE SWEEP VERIFIED, and it vindicates the step-1 deviation. runtime-entrypoint.test.ts passes 3/3 with all three new bridges accepted and none reported as `unexpected`. Had I used the plan's single `doctor-version.test.ts` filename, `doctor-version.node.ts` would have been test-tier and its DoD-5-required bridge would have failed that sweep. The new components module reaches the runtime tier by closure from doctor-version.node.ts, which is itself seeded by its own .test.ts sibling.

READER BEHAVIOUR, as measured on this host: node/platform/arch read live from process and asserted against what the TEST reads from the same API; pnpm resolves through candidate (c), the PATH lookup, and returns 11.0.8. The ladder is (a) npm_execpath when it ends .js/.cjs — empty here even under a real pnpm run, (b) node_modules/pnpm/bin/pnpm.cjs — absent here, (c) PATH filtered through PATHEXT and intersected with a real-image allowlist of .exe/.com. `.cmd`/`.bat`/`.ps1` are excluded because Node 24 cannot spawn them with shell:false; `.js` is excluded too, since a script on PATH is not an executable image. Every spawn: shell:false, windowsHide:true, 10s timeout, 64KB maxBuffer, and exactly one semver-shaped line accepted. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW DONE, COMMITTED BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC, GATE RUN FRESH.

=== ADVERSARIAL PASS — every question from the step, answered by reading the diff ===

1. Can an UNKNOWN render as a satisfied pin? NO, and the guard is structural. `comparePin` and `compareRangePin` both return UNKNOWN on `!declared.known || !observed.known` BEFORE any comparison, so there is no path where an unknown side reaches the equality branch. `ObservedValue` is a two-arm union, so an unreadable value cannot be `undefined` — it is present, coded and layered.

2. Does omitting a value beat supplying a wrong one? NO. Wrong value -> MISMATCHED. Missing value -> UNKNOWN. Neither is SATISFIED, so omission buys nothing. Found and closed one real hole here: `comparePin` is EXPORTED, so a caller could hand it two `{known:true, value:""}` values and blank-equals-blank would have read SATISFIED. contract:168 refuses either side blank as UNKNOWN. The readers already refuse blanks (`value.length > 0` at doctor-version.node.ts:42 and components:47), so this is defence for the exported surface, not a live path.

3. Can a spawn failure escape as a throw? NO. `runVersion` wraps `execFileAsync` in try/catch returning null; every candidate miss falls through; the final miss is `unknown("DOCTOR_TOOL_VERSION_UNREADABLE", HOST)`. Spawn options are `shell:false`, `windowsHide:true`, `maxBuffer: 64KB`, `timeout: 10_000`. `.cmd/.bat/.ps1` are excluded by an ALLOWLIST (`SPAWNABLE_IMAGES = {.exe,.com}` intersected with PATHEXT), not a denylist. `readTextOrNull`, `parseJsonOrNull` and `childDirectories` are each total. `resolveRepoRoot` returns null rather than throwing.

4. Version literals in production source? TWO, both in PROSE COMMENTS, ZERO in executable code — disclosed rather than claimed absent:
  doctor-version-contract.ts:116 ` * \`process.version\` is \`v24.16.0\`; \`.node-version\` is \`24.16.0\\n\`...`
  doctor-version-contract.ts:199 `/** \`pnpm@11.0.8\` is a name AND a version...`
Both document WHY a normalisation exists. `grep -nE "24\.16\.0|11\.0\.8|v24"` over all four production sources returns only those two lines. No literal participates in a comparison; the drills in step 6 proved the readers are read, not restated.

5. Declared vs observed separate on every pin? YES — `VersionPinVerdict` has both as distinct fields and no merged field exists. ONE deliberate exception, flagged for QA: `compareRangePin` REPLACES `declared` with `unknown("DOCTOR_PIN_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED","DOCTOR_VERSION")` when the range grammar is unsupported, so the code and refusing layer travel with the pin. That loses the raw range string. Judged correct — a value this layer cannot interpret is exactly an unreadable declared value — but it IS a substitution and a reviewer should weigh it.

6. Range pin: real check, never string comparison. `satisfiesRange` parses `>=X.Y.Z <A[.B[.C]]` and compares numerically; anything outside that narrow grammar returns null -> coded UNKNOWN. Live probe confirms ENGINES_NODE = SATISFIED against `>=24.16.0 <25`, which a string comparison could never produce.

7. Frozen, and count derived? YES. `Object.isFrozen(report) === true` measured in the plain-Node probe. `componentCount: components.length` at contract:246 — derived, never supplied; `DoctorVersionReportInput` has no count field, so a caller cannot claim a sweep it did not run.
